title: Defense resources, procurement, and co-production precede realized capability and geopolitical leverage
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of SIPRI military expenditure, IMF geopolitical/fiscal scenarios, USAspending defense-award records, and Polish-US defense procurement/co-production announcements
geography: United States, Poland, NATO, and global comparison units retained by source

observations.period: 2025; SIPRI global, national, regional, and NATO military-expenditure estimates

denominator.unit: global military-expenditure aggregate; country and alliance denominators are separate

world_spending.unit: US dollars billions at current prices

world_real_change.unit: percent from 2024 in constant 2024 US dollars

observations.method: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database estimates aggregated by country, region, and NATO grouping using current and constant US-dollar series.
observations.uncertainty: Some country values are estimated; fiscal-year conventions, exchange rates, reporting quality, and classified spending affect comparisons. Spending is an input to capacity, not operational readiness, procurement delivery, or welfare incidence.
observations.subgroup: World, United States, Europe, Asia/Oceania, NATO, and national-spender units.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher allied spending may improve options without producing interoperable capability or timely procurement; a lower US annual total may reflect supplemental-assistance accounting rather than broad capability loss.

observations.period: 2026-2027 and post-World War II defense-boom episodes; IMF April 2026 WEO

denominator.unit: IMF global projection scenario and cross-country defense-boom analysis; historical episodes are not pooled with US observations

typical_defense_outlay_increase.unit: percentage points of GDP over roughly two and a half years

defense_boom_deficit_financing.unit: percent of typical increase financed through deficit

global_growth_2026.unit: percent projected real global growth under April 2026 baseline

observations.method: IMF World Economic Outlook April 2026 defense-spending and conflict chapters, with a limited-duration-conflict baseline and historical cross-country analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Projections and episode averages are conditional and heterogeneous. Financing, import content, domestic slack, allocation, fiscal space, conflict duration, and institutions alter the result; no exact US household or program incidence is estimated.
observations.subgroup: Countries experiencing defense buildups or conflict and global economy projections; country exposure varies by import dependence and fiscal space.
observations.counterinterpretation: Defense spending can raise short-run activity and domestic capacity; imported equipment, financing conditions, and social-spending choices determine distribution and fiscal trade-offs.

observations.period: 2024-10-23 through 2025-02-28; one US DoD JASSM/LRASM parent-award subaward extract

denominator.unit: returned USAspending subaward records linked to one parent award

reported_recipient_count.unit: distinct recipient names in returned records

component_description_coverage.unit: records with one or more component/assembly description terms

observations.method: Official USAspending subaward endpoint retrieval for one parent award; recipient names and reported amounts were aggregated within the returned extract, and free-text component descriptions were coded separately.
observations.uncertainty: The extract is bounded to one parent award and returned endpoint records. It does not establish a complete supply chain, ownership, facility assignment, manufacturing location, workforce, delivery, acceptance, readiness, or supplier competition.
observations.subgroup: Reported subordinate recipients and component/assembly description classes within one JASSM/LRASM award.
observations.counterinterpretation: A multi-recipient extract can indicate distributed sourcing, but may reflect reporting conventions, repeated lots, options, or incomplete visibility; component text is not a bill of materials or delivered-capability measure.

observations.period: 2026-05-13; US Barracuda-500M framework agreement and reported production-capacity route

denominator.unit: Anduril-reported U.S. Department of War framework agreement and associated production-facility disclosure

minimum_us_system_commitment.unit: all-up SLB-500M systems reported for procurement and delivery to the US Army across three years

associated_launcher_start.unit: more than 60 containerized launchers reported to start delivery in 2027

reported_facility_activity.value: 115,000-plus-square-foot Southern California facility opened earlier in 2026 and had begun producing Barracuda variants

reported_capacity_projection.value: high-single-digit-thousands of Barracuda-500 systems by end of 2026

observations.method: Bounded extraction from Anduril's official company release describing a US Department of War framework agreement and associated production investments. The US demand route, facility activity, planned delivery window, and capacity projection are kept separate from verified federal contract performance, accepted output, inventory, and Polish demand.
observations.uncertainty: The source is a contractor disclosure; the underlying federal award, obligation, modification, delivery, acceptance, and facility-output records were not independently matched here. The release does not allocate the US framework quantity to Poland or establish that Polish assembly or production has begun.
observations.subgroup: US Army Program Acquisition Executive FIRES demand route and Anduril's US production-capacity claims for SLB-500M.
observations.counterinterpretation: A framework quantity and reported facility activity can establish a demand and capacity hypothesis without proving funded execution, delivered inventory, operational readiness, or transferability of production/control to a partner country.

observations.period: FY2026; U.S. Department of War Comptroller mandatory funding allocation plan

denominator.unit: official federal funding-allocation plan; program categories are not pooled with product-specific awards

low_cost_cruise_missile_funding.unit: US dollars for development, procurement, and integration of low-cost cruise missiles

lccm_ground_launched_quantity.unit: reported procurement quantity for Low-Cost Containerized Missile-Ground Launched systems

industrial_base_policy.value: testing, procurement, production-rate, and surge-capacity support including allies and partners

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official U.S. Department of War Comptroller FY2026 Mandatory Funding Allocation Plan. Funding, named program categories, quantities, and industrial-base language are retained as an allocation-stage observation rather than matched to a product-specific award.
observations.uncertainty: The plan does not identify Anduril, Barracuda SLB-500M, a recipient, contract line, obligation, production site, delivery, acceptance, or Polish demand. The reported LCCM-GL quantity cannot be assigned to Barracuda without a program-specific federal record.
observations.subgroup: U.S. low-cost cruise-missile and Affordable Mass Munitions funding categories; ally/partner industrial-base language.
observations.counterinterpretation: A federal allocation category can make a capability-development route more plausible while leaving execution, contractor assignment, production, delivery, and operational readiness unresolved.

ordering_requirement.value: orders require separate funding and execution under the vehicle

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the public SAM.gov award notice for Anduril Enterprise Contract W9128Z-26-D-A001. The ceiling, period structure, vehicle type, and broad commercial-offering description are kept separate from product-specific task orders and obligations.
observations.uncertainty: The award notice does not identify Barracuda SLB-500M, a product quantity, task order, obligation, delivery, acceptance, production output, or Polish demand. A same-day USAspending keyword search for exact SLB-500M returned no award match; that non-observation does not prove that no classified or differently described record exists.
observations.subgroup: Anduril federal contract vehicle and authorized ordering agencies; product-specific Barracuda execution remains a separate unit.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large IDIQ ceiling can expand a firm's access to federal demand while remaining unused, broadly scoped, or dependent on later funded orders; it is not evidence of realized missile capability or leverage.

observations.period: 2026-07-28; FAMM-P BAR closed risk-reduction acquisition stage

denominator.unit: official SAM.gov acquisition notice and closed risk-reduction spiral

vendor_access.value: limited to vendors down-selected from the RFI and industry day

follow_on_status.value: possible development-prototype effort subject to approvals and funding; competitive if released

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official SAM.gov AFLCMC ADRR CSO amendment for the Family of Affordable Mass Missiles-Palletized Beyond Adversary's Reach effort. Risk-reduction duration, market-shaping dates, access restriction, CUI distribution, and conditional follow-on language are retained as separate acquisition stages.
observations.uncertainty: The notice does not name Anduril, Barracuda SLB-500M, a selected vendor, a funded prototype, a production quantity, an obligation, delivery, acceptance, or Polish demand. CUI materials are not public in the notice.
observations.subgroup: U.S. Air Force Armament Directorate FAMM-P BAR acquisition route and down-selected vendor set.
observations.counterinterpretation: A closed risk-reduction spiral can narrow technical and vendor options without becoming a production commitment; a possible follow-on remains contingent on approvals, funding, and a future competitive release.

observations.period: FY2026-FY2027; Air Force FAMM00 budget-line justification

denominator.unit: two official Air Force budget exhibits with separate fiscal-year and column contexts

fy2026_mandatory_spend_plan.unit: US dollars; mandatory FAMM spend-plan amount

fy2027_total_request.unit: US dollars; $55M discretionary plus $300M mandatory request

fy2026_p1_exhibit_quantity.unit: reported FAMM quantity in FY2026 Air Force Missile Procurement Exhibit P-1

fy2026_p1_exhibit_cost.unit: US dollars; reported FAMM cost in FY2026 P-1 exhibit columns

multiyear_authorization.unit: years requested for multiyear procurement authorization

observations.method: Non-pooled extraction from the official Air Force FY2027 FAMM00 P-40 justification and FY2026 Air Force Missile Procurement P-1 exhibit. Fiscal-year request, spend-plan, quantity, cost, and multiyear-authorization fields are retained by document and are not summed or treated as obligations.
observations.uncertainty: Budget exhibits contain separate fiscal-year and column contexts; the P-1 quantity/cost and P-40 request figures are not interchangeable. Neither document identifies a task order, obligation, selected vendor, production output, delivery, acceptance, or Polish demand. FAMM-P is not assigned to Barracuda SLB-500M.
observations.subgroup: U.S. Air Force Family of Affordable Mass Missile procurement line; FAMM-P palletized and FAMM-L lugged configurations as described in the justification.
observations.counterinterpretation: A named procurement line and budget request make planned state demand more concrete while remaining subject to appropriation, contracting, design, vendor selection, production, and delivery stages.

observations.period: 2024-2026; Poland-US procurement, reciprocal-access, financing, and Barracuda co-production announcements

denominator.unit: cross-source country-government agreement and follow-up record; each agreement/event retains its own document denominator

jassm_er_agreement_value.unit: US dollars millions, approximate reported 2024 procurement value

barracuda_co_production_partners.value: Poland, United States, Estonia, and Latvia

fmf_agreement_amount.unit: US dollars; broader Poland-US financing agreement, not assigned to Barracuda

observations.method: Deliberately non-pooled extraction of official Polish Ministry of National Defence, Ministry of State Assets, Bydgoszcz government, and National Security Bureau announcements; procurement, financing, implementation terms, targets, and follow-up are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The announcements do not establish plant commissioning, completed units, acceptance, delivery, local-content share, component independence, operational use, public reception, or an external actor changing behavior. The FMF amount has no Barracuda-specific allocation in the cited announcement.
observations.subgroup: Polish defense-industrial and national-security institutions; US, Estonia, Latvia, and regional defense-supply partners.
observations.counterinterpretation: Co-production and buyer/seller language may improve process speed or alliance interoperability while leaving foreign design authority, software, components, approvals, finance, and demand dependence intact. A signed agreement is not realized leverage.

related_sources.claim: SIPRI supplies resource-allocation and alliance-spending context.
IMF WEO supplies conditional defense-boom, fiscal, social-spending, and conflict-risk context.
USAspending supplies a bounded award-to-subaward and component-description route.
Polish official records supply reciprocal-access, co-production, financing, and implementation-stage evidence.
The official FY2026 allocation plan supplies a federal financing and program-category stage for low-cost cruise-missile development without a Barracuda-specific attribution.
The SAM.gov award notice supplies an executed Anduril federal contract vehicle while preserving the difference between a ceiling and a product-specific obligation.
The official FAMM-P BAR notice supplies a closed risk-reduction acquisition stage while preserving the distinction from a funded production award.

The official Air Force FAMM00 budget justification supplies named procurement-line, quantity, request, and multiyear-authorization evidence without establishing a contract obligation or Barracuda attribution.
The official FY2026 Air Force Missile Procurement P-1 exhibit supplies a separate FAMM quantity/cost budget context retained without pooling with the P-40 request.

boundary: This is a non-pooled resource-to-capability bridge. It establishes spending context, conditional fiscal trade-offs, a bounded US award/supplier structure, an executed but broadly scoped Anduril contract vehicle, an official FAMM-P BAR risk-reduction acquisition stage, an official low-cost-cruise-missile financing/program-category stage, a contractor-reported US Barracuda demand/capacity route, and Poland-US agreement-stage industrial responses. It does not establish a product-specific Barracuda obligation, production award, operational capability, domestic household or worker incidence, supplier replaceability, public legitimacy, alliance cohesion, deterrence, bargaining leverage, or changed external behavior. Those require verified product-level orders, production/delivery/acceptance, distributional incidence, control and switching evidence, and an observed state or external response.
